open.title: why-dep defaults to ALL simple paths (not shortest)
open.summary: meow why-dep reports every simple root->target chain by default; --shortest opts into one representative.
open.assumed: Default PathMode::All because a package's full "why" is every owner that pulls it in (matches npm why / cargo tree -i); shortest hides co-owners. Exponential blow-up bounded by --limit (default 256) with an honest truncation note (I-11).

open.title: why-dep root-deps come from the shared declared-deps source, not graph in-degree
open.summary: Assignment said depends_on [PKG-001]; the full CLI honestly needs [PKG-001, PKG-002, CFG-001] because the lockfile cannot mark direct deps.
open.assumed: Per PKG002 IRC, in-degree-zero is wrong (transitive-only pkgs can be in-degree-zero; direct deps can have in-edges). Correct root source = the CFG-owned declared direct deps pinned via meow_pkg::resolve_roots (P2 used a config field; P2.5/CFG-003 moves that authority to package.json). The pure path-finder library stays PKG-001-only.

open.title: Shadow .meow/deps map is flat-by-name; multi-version collisions pick one + record the rest
open.summary: LSP-001's shadow node_modules symlink map exposes one version per package name (CANON §20.1 flat-paths model); multi-version collisions are recorded, not nested.
open.assumed: Flat .meow/deps/<name> over the root-reachable closure matches CANON §20.1's flat tsconfig-paths model; on a multi-version name, link the root-reachable (else lowest) version and record the rest in ShadowDeps::collisions. A nested per-package multi-version tree is a full-LSP refinement; the runtime resolver stays multi-version-correct via the lockfile regardless.

open.title: LSP holds its own Resolver built from the SHARED ResolutionGraph (parity by construction, not a shared Resolver instance)
open.summary: EditorResolver::resolve_module returns the runtime-identical url+locator plus an editor_path into the unpacked store; both sides build their own Resolver from one Arc<ResolutionGraph>.
open.assumed: The Resolver's RefCell PackageFs cache is single-thread (PKG-003), so the LSP and run-path share one Arc<ResolutionGraph> (identical inputs) rather than one Resolver instance. Parity is by construction and asserted by the corpus test. Surface = EditorResolver::resolve_module(specifier, &Url) -> EditorResolution { url, locator, editor_path }.

open.title: Shadow symlink map is Unix-first; Windows (junctions vs --materialize) deferred
open.summary: The prototype ships Unix directory symlinks; Windows directory-symlink support is flagged for the human, not implemented.
open.assumed: Unix directory symlinks (std::os::unix::fs::symlink) ship in the prototype (dev target is darwin). Windows directory symlinks need Developer Mode/privilege; the planned path is directory junctions (no privilege) or falling back to `meow install --materialize`. Committing to junctions vs requiring --materialize on Windows is a product/platform call the full LSP must settle.

open.title: PnP feeds the Resolver by building+validating inputs (ResolutionGraph), not by modifying the resolver
open.summary: meow_pkg::ResolutionGraph (root_deps + Arc<Lockfile> + validated reachable closure) is fed unchanged through the single seam Resolver::from_resolution(&graph, cache, project_root, native); the LOAD-003 algorithm is untouched and node_modules is never read.
open.assumed: The PnP<->Resolver integration fork (ADR-4): PnP is a data producer/validator, not a second resolution path. The resolver already keys first-party off root_deps and cached-referrer deps off LockEntry.dependencies, so PKG-003 only supplies+validates those two inputs. Runtime and LSP build from the SAME Arc<ResolutionGraph> via from_resolution => identical inputs => identical resolution (I-5). node_modules is an export (PKG-004), never consulted (honest boundary, I-11). Coordinated over irc with PKG-004 (consumes ResolutionGraph via packages()), PKG-002 (produces lockfile+cache, owns pin_roots), LSP-001 (constructs only via from_resolution).

open.title: Root direct-dep pins are a pure function of (declared direct deps, lockfile) via resolve_roots; no separate persisted root index
open.summary: ResolutionGraph root_deps come from the SHARED meow_pkg::resolve_roots(direct, lockfile) = max-satisfying locked version per declared direct dep (owned by PKG-002, called by install/runtime/LSP/PnP); no extra on-disk graph artifact beyond package.json-declared roots + meow.lock.jsonl.
open.assumed: The root has no LockEntry, so its exact direct-dep versions need a source. A pure function applied by every consumer cannot diverge (I-5/I-6 by construction). Honest caveat (I-11): max-satisfying lets a root dep silently float to a higher locked patch a transitive pulled in (deterministic, explainable via why-dep/OBS-001). Rejected heavier alternative: an install-written generated .meow/ PnP index (Yarn .pnp.cjs style). Shared root-derivation fn name reconciled to PKG-002's WRITTEN symbol meow_pkg::resolve_roots(direct: BTreeMap<PackageName,DepSpec>, lockfile) -> Result<_, RootResolveError>; P2.5 changes where direct comes from (package.json), not the ResolutionGraph seam.

open.title: PKG-002/PKG-004 default install mode = PnP (ADR-4)
open.summary: meow install defaults to PnP (in-memory, no node_modules); --materialize/--vendor are the escape hatch.
open.assumed: ADR-4 / CANON 24.4 ship PnP + materialize together with PnP as the norm.

open.title: PKG-002 declared deps were a P2 config stopgap; P2.5 moves authority to package.json
open.summary: PKG-002 shipped with declared deps in meow config; Amendment 001/CFG-003 retires that field and makes package.json the dependency authority.
open.assumed: P2 needed a declared-deps source before package.json authority landed. The current architecture is package.json -> resolve_roots -> ResolutionGraph; meow.config remains runtime/tooling/policy only.

open.title: PKG-002 HTTPS registry client = small blocking rustls client at the CLI edge only
open.summary: The real NpmRegistry impl uses a small blocking HTTPS client (e.g. ureq) in the binary edge; meow-pkg stays network-free behind the RegistrySource trait.
open.assumed: Keeps meow-pkg footprint clean (I-10) + testable (FixtureRegistry); the client is swappable.

open.title: PKG-004 node_modules vs vendor = two flags, two projections of one ResolutionGraph
open.summary: --materialize -> node_modules/ (tool-compat, symlink default); --vendor -> vendor/ (full copy, air-gap).
open.assumed: CANON 12.2 defines vendor as a full local copy; modelling both as projections of the shared graph keeps one resolver (I-5).

open.title: PKG-004 isolated/pnpm-style no-hoist materialized layout
open.summary: .meow/<name>@<ver>/node_modules/<name> + per-package relative symlink edges; no hoisting.
open.assumed: Hoisting collapses versions so a foreign Node walker resolves a different version than meow PnP -> breaks resolver-parity (I-5). No-hoist preserves parity.

open.title: PKG-004 link strategy: symlink default (materialize), copy default (vendor), --copy override
open.summary: Edges are symlinks for --materialize, copies for --vendor; --copy forces copies; SymlinkUnsupported is typed (points at --copy), never a silent copy.
open.assumed: Cheapest faithful default per projection; honest typed error on symlink-hostile filesystems.

open.title: PKG-004 vendor = full self-contained copy (resolvable with the global cache absent)
open.summary: vendor/ is a complete copy that resolves air-gapped (global ~/.meow/cache removed), at the cost of disk duplication; an air-gap test is required.
open.assumed: Matches the vendor intent (portable/committable); duplication is the accepted trade.

open.title: Transition to P3 parses once, with DR-003 compatibility contract held fixed
open.summary: Move from P2.5 drop-in Node harvest to P3 parse-once tooling: TOOL-001/002/003 and CHK-001/002 may start, but P2.5 semantics and .meow/deps/editor projection rules remain unchanged.
open.assumed: Runtime truth is still ResolutionGraph + UnpackedStore paths; meow tooling must never bypass that for module identity or compatibility behavior.

resolved.title: Deno owns Node semantics; meow owns the PnP bridge
resolved.summary: Node built-ins, CommonJS semantics, and N-API support move to upstream Deno crates; meow bridges its PnP graph/cache to Deno via real UnpackedStore package paths.
resolved.assumed: Compatibility and UX beat a meow-owned Node reimplementation. Runtime truth is ResolutionGraph; UnpackedStore provides the real filesystem paths Deno's resolver/N-API need; .meow/deps is only the editor/TS/LSP shadow; --materialize is the explicit node_modules escape hatch.
resolved.resolution: Accepted by operator: staged cutover to Deno Node/N-API, with meow as PnP glue and UX/tooling layer; no manual Node polyfills and no synthetic CJS wrappers as target architecture.

resolved.title: PKG-002 version resolution uses the pinned semver crate, not node-semver
resolved.summary: Range resolution uses the workspace semver crate; node-semver-only forms error honestly (NoMatchingVersion/UnsupportedRange) rather than mis-resolve.
resolved.assumed: Avoids a node-semver reimplementation now; the honesty gate (I-11) covers the gap; a faithful engine is a later option.
resolved.resolution: Almost every project is unusable with meow, we actually need to support it fully, and this is adding on to my previous correction of drop-in compat for package.json

resolved.title: PKG-002 integrity: verify npm sha512 on download, content-address by meow sha256 (cache+lockfile key)
resolved.summary: npm dist.integrity (sha512) is the supply-chain check at download; the meow sha256 is the cache key + LockEntry.integrity + I-7 anchor. sha512 verified-then-discarded at P2.
resolved.assumed: PKG-001 cache is sha256; npm SRI is sha512. Verifying npm then content-addressing by sha256 reuses the existing cache without extending HashAlgo; provenance (persist sha512) deferred to SEC-002.
resolved.resolution:
You cannot fight package.json. It isn't just a config file; it is the database of the entire JavaScript ecosystem.
If we strictly enforce ADR-8 (where meow actively overwrites package.json and forces everyone to use meow.config.json), the friction to adopt meow in an existing Next.js, SvelteKit, or Express project is too high. Developers want to clone their existing repo, type meow install, and have it just work.
What "Drop-In Compat" Means for meow
To make meow a true drop-in replacement, we need to adjust the architecture so that it treats package.json as a first-class citizen, not a generated shadow.
Here is what we need the Orchestrator to wire up:
Bidirectional meow install: If a user types meow install svelte in a directory with a package.json, meow reads the existing package.json, resolves the dependency, and writes "svelte": "^5.56.3" directly into package.json (just like npm/bun/pnpm).
First-Class Scripts: meow run dev or meow task build must natively parse the "scripts" block inside package.json. We can keep meow.tasks.ts for advanced, typed task graphs, but standard npm run dev workflows must work out of the box.
Transparent Resolution: The LOAD-003 resolver we just built needs to treat package.json's dependencies and devDependencies as the root of the module graph if meow.config.json doesn't explicitly override it.
